name: Nusinersen
route_note: Intrathecal injection by lumbar puncture: four loading doses, then maintenance every four months.
originator: Ionis Pharmaceuticals (Isis) with Adrian Krainer (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory); developed with Biogen

discovery.by: Adrian Krainer (Cold Spring Harbor) and Frank Bennett (Isis Pharmaceuticals)
discovery.note: A 2'-O-methoxyethyl phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide designed to block an intronic splicing silencer and promote inclusion of SMN2 exon 7.

tagline: First approved treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, a splice-correcting antisense drug
summary: Nusinersen was the first disease-modifying treatment for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). By altering splicing of the backup SMN2 gene it increases production of full-length SMN protein, improving motor milestones and survival, particularly when started early.
mechanism: SMA is caused by loss of the SMN1 gene. The nearly identical SMN2 gene mostly produces a truncated, unstable protein because exon 7 is skipped during splicing.

Nusinersen binds the intronic splicing silencer N1 (ISS-N1) in intron 7 of SMN2 pre-mRNA, displacing repressor proteins (hnRNP A1/A2) so that exon 7 is included. This increases full-length SMN protein in motor neurons. Because the oligonucleotide does not cross the blood–brain barrier, it is given intrathecally.
uses: Spinal muscular atrophy (5q SMA) in children and adults

history.title: SMN1 gene
history.detail: Lefebvre et al. identify SMN1 as the SMA-determining gene.

history.title: ENDEAR halted early and FDA approval
history.detail: Interim results in infant-onset SMA lead to early trial termination; the FDA approves Spinraza in December.

history.title: EU approval and publications
history.detail: The EU authorises Spinraza; ENDEAR (Finkel et al.) and CHERISH (Mercuri et al., 2018) are published in NEJM.

history.title: Breakthrough Prize
history.detail: Adrian Krainer and Frank Bennett receive the Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences for developing nusinersen.

history.title: NURTURE
history.detail: Presymptomatic treatment results show most infants achieving walking, supporting newborn screening for SMA.

common: Post-lumbar puncture headache and back pain

facts: Its US launch price of $125,000 per injection made nusinersen one of the most expensive drugs at the time.
Nusinersen was one of the first splice-switching antisense drugs approved anywhere.
